1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16.

2.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02). This also occurs in verses 12 and 21.

2.q: אֱמֹר֩ לִ⁠נְגִ֨יד צֹ֜ר כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהֹוִ֗ה
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [give the ruler of Tyre this message from the Lord Yahweh]

The word **Because** introduces the reason for the judgment that Yahweh will announce in verse 7. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what Yahweh says he will do.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the ruler’s **heart** were something that could be **high**. It means that the ruler of Tyre has been very proud. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Because you have been very proud]

The implication is that the ruler of Tyre was claiming that his island city, surrounded by the sea, was a home for a god, and that he himself was that god. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [my island city in the heart of the seas is the dwelling of God, and I, God, have dwelt in it]
See how you translated this expression in 27:4. This also occurs in verse 8.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the ruler had **given** his **heart** so that it would be like **the heart of God**. It means that the ruler considered himself as being as wise as God. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have considered yourself to be as wise as God]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4. This also occurs in verses 6, 12, 22, and 25.

3.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. He is mocking the ruler of Tyre, who thinks that he is **wiser than Daniel**. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Behold, you think that you are wiser than Daniel]

Yahweh is using **they have not darkened** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they have not hidden.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they have not kept any secret from you]

The pronoun **they** does not refer to any specific people. It refers to people in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [every hidden thing no one has darkened from you]

4.note: The terms **wisdom** and **understanding** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [By your great wisdom]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if wealth were something that Tyre could **made** like a manufactured object. It means that the ruler of Tyre acquired gold and silver and stored them in his treasuries. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have gathered gold and silver into your treasuries]

5.note: If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **abundance** and **wisdom**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Because you are very wise]
See how you translated the similar phrase in verse 2. Alternate translation: [and you have been very proud because of your wealth]

6.note: The word **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before in verses 2 through 5. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [So]

By **your giving your heart as the heart of God**, Yahweh means that the ruler of Tyre thinks he is as wise as God is (or the gods are, the Hebrew can go either way). You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your considering yourself as wise as God]

7.note: **Behold me** is an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [now I am about to bring]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if **the beauty of your wisdom** were something that enemies could attack with **swords**. It means that the enemies will destroy the beautiful things that the ruler of Tyre had gained by his wisdom. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will destroy the beautiful things that you gained by your wisdom]

Yahweh is using the adjective **ruthless** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the most ruthless people of the nations]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the ruler’s **radiance** were a holy thing that the enemies would **profane**. It means that the enemies will ruin the splendor of the ruler and bring him disgrace. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they will ruin your splendor and disgrace you]

8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the place of the dead were a deep **pit** into which enemies would **bring you down**. It means that the enemies will kill the ruler of Tyre. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They will kill you]

Yahweh is using **die the deaths of a slain one** as a common expression of the culture to mean “die a violent death, like someone killed in battle.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will die violently like someone killed in battle]

9.q: הֶ⁠אָמֹ֤ר תֹּאמַר֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אָ֔נִי לִ⁠פְנֵ֖י הֹֽרְגֶ֑⁠ךָ
9.note: Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis. He means that the ruler will certainly not claim to be God when his enemies are about to kill him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You will certainly not say, ‘I am a god,’ to the face of the ones killing you!]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **say** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Will you really say]

Here, **face** represents “presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of the ones killing you]

Here, **hand** represents “power” or “control.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [under the power of the ones piercing you]

10.note: The implication is that to die **an uncircumcised death** was to die a shameful death, since people who were not circumcised were unclean and outside of God’s covenant. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You will die the shameful deaths of those who are unclean and outside of God’s covenant]

By **for I, I have spoken**, Yahweh means that what he has just said will certainly happen because he himself has declared it. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself have spoken]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:21.

12.note: See how you translated these same phrases in [Ezekiel 19:1](ta:19). Alternate translation: [sing a lamentation]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the king of Tyre were a seal that a person would use to stamp a design. In saying that the king was **the sealer of a pattern**, Yahweh may mean either (1) that the king was a seal of perfection, that is, a perfect example of what a king should be, Alternate translation: [You were a perfect example of what a king should be] or (2) that the king was like a signet of perfect design, a beautiful and valuable object. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You were like a beautiful signet ring]
If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **wisdom** and **beauty**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [very wise and perfectly beautiful]

13.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the king of Tyre had lived **In Eden, the garden of God**. It means that the king had been in a place of great beauty, wealth, and blessing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You lived in a place as beautiful and rich as Eden, the garden of God]

Yahweh is speaking as if precious stones were a garment that was the king’s **covering**. It means that the king wore and possessed many kinds of jewels. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You adorned yourself with every kind of precious stone]

13.q: אֹ֣דֶם פִּטְדָ֞ה וְ⁠יָהֲלֹ֗ם תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ שֹׁ֨הַם֙ וְ⁠יָ֣שְׁפֵ֔ה סַפִּ֣יר נֹ֔פֶךְ וּ⁠בָרְקַ֖ת
13.note: The words **ruby**, **topaz**, **diamond**, **beryl**, **onyx**, **jasper**, **sapphire**, **emerald**, and **garnet** are names of kinds of precious stones. If your readers would not be familiar with these stones, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [nine different kinds of beautiful gems]

The meaning of these words is uncertain. Yahweh may be referring to (1) the gem settings and mountings in which the precious stones were placed, Alternate translation: [Skilled craftsmen made your settings and mountings of gold for you] or (2) tambourines and other musical instruments that were made for the king. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Skilled craftsmen made musical instruments for you]

**They were prepared** and **your being created** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the actions, God did them. Alternate translation: [In the day when God created you he prepared them]

14.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the king of Tyre were a **cherub** that he anointed and that covered or guarded Yahweh’s presence. It means that Yahweh appointed the king to a position of great honor and authority, like a guardian creature that stood close to Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You were like a cherub that I appointed to protect my throne] or [You were a highly honored guardian whom I set apart]

The phrase **You were a cherub of anointing, the one covering. And I placed you** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense because the word for “You were” is feminine, while the rest of the passage addresses a masculine person. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [And I placed you with the cherub, the one covering. You were]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean a cherub whom Yahweh anointed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [a cherub that I anointed] or [an anointed cherub]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **mountain** that is characterized by **holiness** and that belongs to **God**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the holy mountain that belongs to God]

Yahweh is speaking as if the king lived among **the stones of fire**, glowing stones in the place where God was present. It means that the king had been very close to the presence of God and had enjoyed great honor. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you lived very close to my presence and enjoyed great honor]

15.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the way the king lived were a set of **ways**, or paths, that he walked along. It means that the king behaved in a blameless way. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You lived a blameless life]

15.q: מִ⁠יּ֖וֹם הִבָּֽרְאָ֑⁠ךְ עַד נִמְצָ֥א עַוְלָ֖תָ⁠ה בָּֽ⁠ךְ
15.note: The expressions **your being created** and **injustice was found** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the first action, God did it. Alternate translation: [from the day that God created you until you started acting unjustly]

16.note: The pronoun **They** does not have a clear antecedent. It may refer to either (1) people in general, in which case you could express this in another way, Alternate translation: [Your midst was filled with] or [Violence filled your midst] or (2) the king’s traders, who acted violently while they carried on trade. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Your traders filled your midst with violence]

Yahweh is speaking as if **violence** were a substance that could fill a container, and as if the king’s **midst** were that container. It means that there was a great deal of violence in the king’s city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They did many violent things in your city]

Yahweh is speaking as if the king were something holy that God **profaned**, that is, treated as unclean, and then removed **from the mountain of God**. It means that God disgraced the king and drove him away from his place of honor. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I disgraced you and drove you away from your place of honor]

The phrase **and I made you perish O cherub** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. However if you chose to follow the Greek text in verse 14, you may want to follow it here as well. Alternate translation: [and the cherub expelled you]

17.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the king’s **heart** were something that could be **high**. It means that the king was proud because of his **beauty**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You were proud because of your beauty]

If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **beauty** and **radiance**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [because you were so beautiful you ruined your wisdom because you were so radiant]

Yahweh is speaking as if he had picked up the king and **threw** him to the ground. It means that Yahweh removed the king from his high position and humiliated him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I removed you from your high position and humiliated you]

The implication is that Yahweh made the king a public spectacle, so that other kings would see how he had been humiliated and would be warned by what happened to him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I made you a spectacle before other kings, so that they would look upon your humiliation and be warned]

18.note: The implication is that **your sanctuaries** refers to the temples in the city of Tyre, and that the king made them unholy by his many sins and his dishonest trade. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You made the temples in your city unholy]

If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **iniquities** and **injustice**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Because you acted wickedly so often, by cheating others when you traded]

The point of this comparison is that just as **ashes** are what remains after something has been completely burned up, so was the king of Tyre after Yahweh’s fire consumed him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And I made you as insignificant as ashes on the earth]

Here, **the eyes** represent “sight.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the sight of all the ones seeing you]

19.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 27:36.

21.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in Ezekiel 4:3. Alternate translation: [make your face firm to Sidon]

22.note: Yahweh is telling Ezekiel to speak to the city of **Sidon**, which cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to Ezekiel that he feels very strongly about his judgment of Sidon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about Sidon. Alternate translation: [Behold, I am against you people of Sidon]

Here, **against you, Sidon** represents the people of Sidon, since Yahweh is speaking to the city but means the people who live there. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Behold, I am against you people of Sidon]

The expression **I will be glorified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh himself is the one who will show his glory by what he does to Sidon. Alternate translation: [and I will display my glory in your midst]

The pronoun **they** refers to people in general, including the people of Sidon and the people of other nations who will see what Yahweh does. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people of Sidon and of other nations will know that I am Yahweh]

The implication is that when these things happen, the people will recognize that Yahweh is the true God, who has the power and authority to do what he has said he will do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the Introduction to Ezekiel for more information. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, am the true God who has the power to do what I said I would do]

Even though Yahweh is addressing Sidon directly, he speaks of the city in the third person as **her**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [when I do judgments in you and I am sanctified in you]

The expression **I am sanctified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh himself is the one who will show that he is holy by judging Sidon. Alternate translation: [and I show that I am holy in her]

23.note: Here, **blood** represents “bloodshed,” that is, people being killed violently. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [plague and violent killing in her streets]

Here, **fall** represents “die,” and **the sword** represents enemy soldiers who kill people in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the slain will die in her midst by the attack of enemy soldiers]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **slain one**. He means slain people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the slain people will fall in her midst]

24.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03).

Yahweh is speaking as if the nations around Israel were **a pricking brier and a thorn causing pain**. It means that these nations had harmed and troubled the Israelites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [anyone who harms and troubles them]

25.note: The expression **they were scattered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, Yahweh did it. Alternate translation: [among whom I had dispersed them]

The expression **I am sanctified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh himself is the one who will show that he is holy by what he does for the Israelites. Alternate translation: [and I show that I am holy among them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:8.
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:15. Alternate translation: [that I promised to give to the descendants of my servant Jacob]

26.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **security**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And they will dwell on it and be secure]
